akhfash:4-4.t: He said ﴿خُشُبٌ مُّسَنَّدَةٌ﴾, just as one says "عَمَدٌ" and "عُمُدٌ"; it is like "الخُشُب", and some of them say "الخُشْبُ".

akhfash:5-5.t: [And He said] ﴿لَوَّوْاْ رُءُوسَهُمْ﴾ (with a doubled wāw) because in the speech of the Arabs, when it concerns mockery or multiplicity, one says ﴿لَوَّى لِسَانَه﴾ ("he twisted his tongue") and "رأسَه" ("his head"). Some read it light (without doubling) and cited as proof the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿لَيّاً بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ﴾.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِذَا جَاءَكَ الْمُنَافِقُونَ قَالُوا﴾ with their tongues, contrary to what is in their hearts, ﴿نَشْهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ﴾ knows ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ in what they concealed, contrary to what they said.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً﴾ a cover over their property and their blood, ﴿فَصَدُّوا﴾ by means of them ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. from fighting against them. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ سَاءَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾, i.e. the evil of their deeds, ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا﴾ with the tongue ﴿ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا﴾ with the heart, i.e. persisted in their disbelief in it; ﴿فَطُبِعَ﴾ a seal was set ﴿عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ with disbelief, ﴿فَهُمْ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ faith.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ أَجْسَامُهُمْ﴾ for their beauty, ﴿وَإِنْ يَقُولُوا تَسْمَعْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ﴾ for its eloquence; ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾, owing to the bulk of their bodies, in their lack of understanding, ﴿خُشْبٌ﴾ — with sukūn on the shīn and with ḍamma [خُشُبٌ] — ﴿مُسَنَّدَةٌ﴾ leaned against the wall. ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ﴾ that is shouted, such as a call in the army camp or the crying out for a lost animal, ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, because of the terror in their hearts that something might be revealed about them making their blood lawful. ﴿هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ فَاحْذَرْهُمْ﴾, for they divulge your secret to the disbelievers. ﴿قَاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ may He destroy them! ﴿أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ how are they turned away from faith after the proof has been established?

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا﴾ apologising, ﴿يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ لَوَّوْا﴾ — with tashdīd and without it — they turned ﴿رُءُوسَهُمْ وَرَأَيْتَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ﴾ turning away from that ﴿وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ﴾: the interrogative hamza suffices in place of the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl); ﴿أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ لَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿هُمُ الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ﴾ to their companions among the Helpers, ﴿لَا تُنْفِقُوا عَلَى مَنْ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ﴾ of the Emigrants ﴿حَتَّى يَنْفَضُّوا﴾ disperse from him. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ خَزَائِنُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ with provision; so He is the Provider for the Emigrants and others; ﴿وَلَكِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿يَقُولُونَ لَئِنْ رَجَعْنَا﴾, i.e. from the raid on the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, ﴿إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ﴾ — by it they meant themselves — ﴿مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ﴾ — by it they meant the believers. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ﴾ the dominance ﴿وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَكِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُلْهِكُمْ﴾ distract you ﴿أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُكُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ the five prayers. ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا﴾ in zakat ﴿مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلَا﴾ in the sense of هَلَّا (why not), or the lā is redundant (zāʾida) and law is for wishing, ﴿أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ﴾ — with assimilation of the tāʾ, originally, into the ṣād — I would give charity with zakat, ﴿وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ by performing the pilgrimage. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: No one falls short in zakat and the pilgrimage except that he asks for a return at death.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَلَنْ يُؤَخِّرَ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهَا وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِذا جاءَكَ﴾ «إذا» is an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive, and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْمُنافِقُونَ﴾ its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿نَشْهَدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and its khabar (predicate), annexed to the Name of Majesty, and the nominal clause is the answer to «نشهد», with no grammatical position, because it is treated like an oath. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of parenthesis, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun, and the shifted lām; ﴿رسوله﴾ its khabar; and «إنّ» with its noun and khabar stands in place of the two objects of «يعلم». ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَشْهَدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun, and the shifted lām; ﴿كاذبون﴾ its khabar.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَيْمانَهُمْ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿جُنَّةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَصَدُّوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿صدوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿ساءَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿ما﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause «ساء» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». ﴿كانُوا﴾ «كان» and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «كانوا».

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition, and «أنّ» and its noun; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause «آمنوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «أنّ»; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أنّ» and what follows it is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the bāʾ, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause «ذلك..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَطُبِعَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿رَأَيْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿تُعْجِبُكَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿أَجْسامُهُمْ﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and the clause «إذا..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ «إن» is conditional and makes the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the wāw being its fāʿil; ﴿تَسْمَعْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); ﴿لِقَوْلِهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ﴾ «كأنّ», its noun and its khabar (predicate); ﴿مُسَنَّدَةٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, annexed to «صيحة»; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿فَاحْذَرْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is the apodosis of the implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَنَّى﴾ an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is conjunctive; ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿تَعالَوْا﴾ an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿يَسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ fāʿil, annexed to the Name of Majesty, and the clause is the answer to the request, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَوَّوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿رُؤُسَهُمْ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا», with no grammatical position. ﴿وَرَأَيْتَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَصُدُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿سَواءٌ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سواء»; ﴿أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ﴾ the hamza is for equivalence (taswiya), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from the hamza and what follows it is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَمْ﴾ the correlative (muʿādila); ﴿لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لم», whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. And the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَنْ يَغْفِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «لن»; ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the verbal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ «إنّ», the Name of Majesty being its noun; ﴿لا يَهْدِي﴾ «لا» is negating, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْفاسِقِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «القوم», and the verbal clause is the khabar of «إنّ», and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿هُمُ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لا تُنْفِقُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿عَلى مَنْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ﴾ an adverb of place annexed to «رسول», the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition; ﴿يَنْفَضُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after «حتى», the wāw being its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by «حتى», and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to «تنفقوا». And the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿وَلِلَّهِ﴾ a fronted khabar; ﴿خَزائِنُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿وَلكِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ «لكنّ» and its noun; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «لكنّ», and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined in meaning to what precedes it; ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ the lām paves the way for an omitted oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); ﴿إن﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive; ﴿رَجَعْنا﴾ a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), «نا» being its fāʿil, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿لَيُخْرِجَنَّ﴾ the lām falls in the answer to the oath, and an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; ﴿الْأَعَزُّ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَذَلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿الْعِزَّةُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَلِرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «لله»; ﴿وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ conjoined to «لله». ﴿وَلكِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ «لكنّ» and its noun; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «لكنّ», and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), and «ها» is for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»; ﴿لا تُلْهِكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the kāf being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَمْوالُكُمْ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it, and the clause is also initial, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مَنْ يَفْعَلْ﴾ «من» is a conditional noun making the verb jussive, mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿أولئك﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿هُمُ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْخاسِرُونَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «أولئك», and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of «من». And the clause «من يفعل..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنْ ما﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿رَزَقْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ both are attached to «أنفقوا»; ﴿أَنْ يَأْتِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن»; ﴿أَحَدَكُمُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْمَوْتُ﴾ fāʿil, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and what follows it is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿فَيَقُولَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يأتي», accusative like it, its fāʿil being latent (mustatir); ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf); ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning «هلّا»; ﴿أَخَّرْتَنِي﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إِلى أَجَلٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿قَرِيبٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «أجل», and the verbal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَأَصَّدَّقَ﴾ the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implicit «أن» after the fāʾ, the fāʿil being latent; the interpreted maṣdar made from «أن» and the verb is conjoined by the fāʾ to a preceding interpreted maṣdar; ﴿وَأَكُنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by being conjoined to the position of «فأصدق», its noun being latent; ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَلَنْ يُؤَخِّرَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «لن»; ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty is fāʿil (agent); ﴿نَفْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِذا جاءَ أَجَلُها﴾ an adverb of time, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿بِما﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خبير»; ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(إِذا جاءَكَ الْمُنافِقُونَ قالُوا نَشْهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ) إذا is an adverb for future time, putting its protasis in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis. The clause جاءك is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and المنافقون is the fāʿil (agent) of جاءك. The clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and it is what governs the adverb. The clause نشهد is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). إنّ and its noun; the hamza of إنّ takes kasra because the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) enters upon its khabar (predicate); رسول الله is the khabar of إنّ. The meaning of نشهد is "we swear", so it functions like an oath.
(وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لَكاذِبُونَ) The wāw is parenthetical; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يعلم the khabar, and the clause is parenthetical between their saying نشهد إنك لرسول الله and His saying والله يشهد. إنّ and its noun, the shifted lām, and رسوله is the khabar; إنّ with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يعلم, and its hamza takes kasra only because the lām occurs entering upon the khabar. الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يشهد the khabar; إنّ and its noun, the shifted lām, and كاذبون its khabar.
(اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ جُنَّةً فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) اتخذوا is a verb and its fāʿil; أيمانهم is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is the plural of يمين (oath); جنة is a second mafʿūl bihi, i.e. a protection and a shield. The clause is new (mustaʾnafa), set out to explain their lying and their swearing to it. Swearing was expressed as "bearing witness" because each of the two is an affirmation of a specific matter. The fāʾ is a conjunction; صدّوا is a verb and its fāʿil, and عن سبيل الله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) صدّوا.
(إِنَّهُمْ ساءَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) إنّ and its noun, and the clause ساء is the khabar; ما is the fāʿil of ساء, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause); كان and its noun, and the clause يعملون is the khabar of كان.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا فَطُبِعَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لا يَفْقَهُونَ) ذلك is a mubtadaʾ; the bāʾ is a preposition, and أنّ with what it governs is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of ذلك, i.e. "because of their believing and then their disbelieving". The fāʾ is a conjunction; طبع is a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; على قلوبهم is attached to طبع. The fāʾ is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يفقهون is the khabar.

dervis-irab:4-6.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا رَأَيْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ أَجْسامُهُمْ وَإِنْ يَقُولُوا تَسْمَعْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb for future time; the clause رأيتهم is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis, which is تعجبك. The clause تعجبك أجسامهم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition. The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional and يقولوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). تسمع is the apodosis, and لقولهم is attached to تسمع; تسمع must be made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of "incline your ear, lean towards", to justify its taking an object with the lām.
(كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ) The clause is new (mustaʾnafa), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in قولهم. كأنّ, its noun and its khabar; مسندة is a naʿt (adjective) of خشب. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «الخشب (wood) is well known; the singular is خشبة; and الخُشُب with two ḍammas, or with the second [letter] quiescent».
(يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ فَاحْذَرْهُمْ) The clause is likewise new. يحسبون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; كل صيحة is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and عليهم is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of يحسبون, i.e. "being against them". هم is a mubtadaʾ and العدو the khabar, and the clause is new. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you have recognised their description and the nature of their states, then beware of them". It is also permissible for the second object of يحسبون to be His saying هم العدو, in which case عليهم is attached to صيحة or is an adjective of it.
(قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ) قاتلهم is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi, and الله is the fāʿil. أنّى means "how", so it is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; يؤفكون is a passive imperfect verb. The meaning of قاتلهم الله is "may Allah curse them".
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعالَوْا يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ لَوَّوْا رُؤُسَهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb, and the clause قيل is in the position of genitive by annexation to it [Translator's note: i.e. by the adverb's annexation to it]; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), and لهم is attached to قيل. تعالوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). يستغفر is the apodosis of the command, jussive (majzūm) with sukūn; لكم is attached to يستغفر and رسول الله is the fāʿil. والواو is a past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «لوّوا» is a past verb], and the wāw is the fāʿil; it has also been read with the lightened form (لَوَوْا), i.e. they turned their heads and inclined them. رءوسهم is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of إذا. Al-Samīn's words are: «The grammarians counted this question among [the cases of] al-iʿmāl (rivalry of two governors), in that تعالوا requires رسول الله as genitive with إلى, i.e. "come to the Messenger of Allah", and يستغفر requires it as fāʿil; so the second was made to govern, and that is why it is nominative, and the [complement of the] first was omitted, since the implied form is "come to him". Had the first been made to govern, it would have been said "to the Messenger of Allah", and a fāʿil would be implied as a pronoun in يستغفر. It may be said that this is not a case of al-iʿmāl at all, because His saying تعالوا is a command to come forward as such, without regard to someone towards whom one comes».
(وَرَأَيْتَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; رأيتهم is a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, the seeing being visual. The clause يصدّون is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in رأيتهم, and the clause وهم مستكبرون is a ḥāl of the wāw in يصدّون.
(سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ) سواء is a fronted khabar, and عليهم is attached to سواء. The hamza is for equalisation (taswiya), and its discussion has preceded; together with what follows it, it is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) which is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The interrogative hamza has dispensed with the hamzat al-waṣl, i.e. "your seeking forgiveness and its absence are alike". لهم is attached to استغفرت. أم is the one that balances the hamza of equalisation (al-muʿādila); لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; تستغفر is an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, and لهم is attached to تستغفر.
(لَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ) لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; يغفر is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن, and الله is the fāʿil; لهم is attached to تغفر [sic]. إنّ and its noun, and the clause لا يهدي is its khabar; القوم is a mafʿūl bihi and الفاسقين a naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying كأنهم خشب مسنّدة there is a loose (mursal) representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī). The thing likened is "them", i.e. the leaders of the hypocrites of Medina: they used to attend the gathering of the Prophet ﷺ and lean against the walls in it, and the Prophet and those present used to marvel at their upright frames. The thing it is likened to is upright timbers propped against the wall. The point of resemblance is that both sides are figures empty of knowledge and reflection, in the vein of Ḥassān's saying:
لا بأس بالقوم من طول ومن عظم ... جسم البغال وأحلام العصافير
(There is nothing wrong with the people as to height and bulk: the bodies of mules and the minds of sparrows.)
In His saying «يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم» there is also a representational simile: because of their cowardice, the panic of their souls and the agitation of their hearts, whenever a caller calls out in the camp, or a beast breaks loose, or a stray animal is cried for, their hearts pound and their good sense deserts them, and they think that there is some evil lying in wait for them and some plot waiting to fall upon their lives. Al-Akhṭal gazed at the heights of this meaning and said:
ما زلت تحسب كلّ شيء بعدهم ... خيلا تكرّ عليهم ورجالا
(After them you kept thinking every thing to be horsemen and footmen charging upon them.)
Al-Akhṭal is saying: O Jarīr, after your people were forsaken you have not ceased to think every thing to be horsemen charging, i.e. returning swiftly upon them, because of how much fear besets you. Al-Mutanabbī went to excess with this meaning and said:
وضاقت الأرض حتى صار هاربهم ... إذا رأى غير شيء ظنه رجلا
(The earth grew narrow until their fugitive, when he saw nothing at all, took it to be a man.)
It may also be said that the point of resemblance is the absence of their minds and the emptiness of their hearts of faith. He was not content with the comparison to timbers, but made them propped against the wall for being used [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense required is evidently "not for being used", i.e. idle], because if they were in a roof or a [proper] place they would be used.

dervis-irab:7-11.t:
* I'rab:
(هُمُ الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لا تُنْفِقُوا عَلى مَنْ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ حَتَّى يَنْفَضُّوا) A new (mustaʾnaf) statement functioning as an explanation of the cause of their depravity. هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذين the khabar (predicate); the clause يقولون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. لا is prohibitive; تنفقوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). على من is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنفقوا; the adverb [عند] is attached to an omitted element having no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of من; رسول الله is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). حتى is a particle of cause and accusative; ينفضّوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the meaning is "so that they disperse", i.e. each one of them goes off on his own way and his own business.
(وَلِلَّهِ خَزائِنُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لله is a fronted khabar and خزائن السموات والأرض a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَلكِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لا يَفْقَهُونَ) لكنّ and its noun, and the clause لا يفقهون is its khabar.
(يَقُولُونَ لَئِنْ رَجَعْنا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ) A statement conjoined in meaning to the preceding يقولون, because the occasion of the two sayings is one. The lām paves the way for an oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); إن is conditional, and رجعنا is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); إلى المدينة is attached to رجعنا. The lām occurs in the response to the oath; يخرجنّ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, necessarily; الأعزّ is its fāʿil and الأذلّ its object. By "the mightier" they meant themselves, and by "the more abject" Muḥammad ﷺ. منها is attached to يخرجنّ.
(وَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلكِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The wāw is circumstantial; لله is a fronted khabar and العزّة a postponed mubtadaʾ; ولرسوله is conjoined to لله. As for ولكن: the wāw is a conjunction, then لكنّ and its noun, and the clause لا يعلمون is its khabar.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُلْهِكُمْ أَمْوالُكُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ) يا is a vocative particle for one at middle distance; أيّ is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of accusative; the hāʾ is for drawing attention, and الذين is a badal (substitute); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila. لا is prohibitive; تلهكم is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; أموالكم is the fāʿil, ولا أولادكم is conjoined to أموالكم, and عن ذكر الله is attached to تلهكم.
(وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussivizing conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and ذلك is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, and هم is a second mubtadaʾ or a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); الخاسرون is the khabar of أولئك, or the khabar of هم with the clause being the khabar of أولئك. The clause فأولئك etc. is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.
(وَأَنْفِقُوا مِنْ ما رَزَقْناكُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ) The wāw is a conjunction; أنفقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; مما is attached to أنفقوا, من being partitive, and what is meant is obligatory spending. The clause رزقناكم has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila. من قبل is a ḥāl; أن and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the genitive by annexation. أحدكم is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and الموت a postponed mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; الموت is in fact the postponed fāʿil of يأتي].
(فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلا أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) The fāʾ is the conjunctive fāʾ of causation, because [the saying] is caused by أن يأتي. يقول is an imperfect verb conjoined to أن يأتي, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring back to أحدكم. لولا is for urging (taḥḍīḍ), meaning هلّا; أخّرتني is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, but it has the meaning of the imperfect, because the لولا of urging is specific to the past verb interpreted as imperfect, since there is no sense in asking for postponement in past time. The tāʾ is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; إلى أجل is attached to أخّرتني, and قريب is a naʿt (adjective). The fāʾ in فأصدّق is a conjunction [Translator's note: so in the source]; أكن is an imperfect verb, jussive by being conjoined to the position (maḥall) of فأصدّق, as if it were said "if You postpone me, I will give charity and be". It has been read with أكونَ in the accusative and with the wāw retained, in which case the wāw is for causation [Translator's note: so in the source], and أصدّق is accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation in response to the request, i.e. the urging. The noun of أكن is latent, its implied form being "I", and من الصالحين is its khabar.
(وَلَنْ يُؤَخِّرَ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِذا جاءَ أَجَلُها وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the statement is conjoined to something implied, i.e. "so this wishing person will not be given respite, because He does not give respite to any soul, whichever it may be, when its term has come". لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; يؤخر is an imperfect verb, accusative by لن; الله is the fāʿil and نفسا the mafʿūl bihi. إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition, and the clause جاء أجلها is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "He will not give respite to a soul whose time has come". الله is a mubtadaʾ, خبير the khabar, and بما is attached to خبير; the clause تعملون is the ṣila of ما. It has also been read يعملون with the yāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعزّ منها الأذل» there is a figure called al-qawl bi-l-mūjab (turning the opponent's statement against him). It is that a speaker addresses someone with a statement, and the one addressed takes up each individual word of the speaker's statement and builds upon it, from his own words, what entails the opposite of the speaker's meaning; for the reality of al-qawl bi-l-mūjab is that an opponent refutes his adversary's statement from the purport of that statement itself. What the hypocrites' saying, mentioned above in the verse, entails is the Messenger's expelling the hypocrites from Medina, and that did happen. Do you not see that Allah the Exalted said directly after it: «ولله العزّة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون»? Among its examples is the saying of Ibn Ḥajjāj al-Baghdādī:
قلت: ثقلت إذ أتيت مرارا ... قال: ثقلت كاهلي بالأيادي
قلت: طولت قال لي: بل تطو ... لت وأبرمت قال: حبل ودادي
(I said: "I have been a burden, coming so often." He said: "You have burdened my shoulders with favours." I said: "I have been long-winded." He said to me: "Rather, you have been generous." [I said:] "And I have wearied you." He said: "[You have made firm] the rope of my affection.")

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾.
Someone may say: They bore witness for the Prophet ﷺ, saying: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ﴾, so how did Allah call them liars?
It is said: He only gave the lie to what they concealed in themselves, because they concealed hypocrisy. Just as He did not accept their faith although they displayed it, so He made them liars, because they concealed something other than what they displayed.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّالِحِينَ﴾.
It is asked: How is (وأكن) jussive when it is joined back to an accusative verb? The answer to that is that if the فاء had not been on أصدق, it would have been jussive; so when you joined (وأكنْ) back, it was joined to the underlying sense of the verb as it would be without the فاء. Whoever keeps the واو joins it back to the overt verb and so makes it accusative; and that is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وأكونَ من الصالحين".
Its accusative is also permissible in our reading even though the واو is not in it [in the script], because the Arabs sometimes drop the واو in some spellings, just as they dropped the ألف from سليمن and the like. I have seen in some of the codices of ʿAbd Allāh: فقولا written فقلا, without واو.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ أَجْسَامُهُمْ﴾.
Some of the Arabs put the verb in the jussive after إذا, saying: إذا تقم أقمْ (when you stand, I stand). One of them recited to me:
وإذا نطاوِعْ أمرَ سادتِنا * لا يَثْنِنا جُبن ولا بُخْلُ
(When we obey the command of our lords, neither cowardice nor miserliness turns us back.)
Another said:
واستغْنِ ما أغناك ربُّك بالغِنى * وإذا تُصبْك خصاصةٌ فتجمَّل
(Be content with wealth as long as your Lord makes you rich; and when poverty strikes you, bear it with dignity.)
But most usage with it is the nominative [indicative], because it is in the manner of an adverbial (ṣifa, i.e. ẓarf), do you not see that you say: الرُّطب إذا اشتد الحر (fresh dates are when the heat grows intense), meaning at that time. Since it is in the position of an adverbial, it is a complement (ṣila) of the verb that comes before it, or of what comes after the verb that follows it. So the poet said:
وإذا تكون شديدةٌ أُدْعَى لها * وإذا يحاسُ الحَيْسُ يُدْعَى جُندُبُ
(When there is a hardship, I am called for it; and when the ḥays [a date-and-butter dish] is mixed, Jundub is called.)
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُّسَنَّدَةٌ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read it light [خُشْب], and Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar al-Madanī, from his companions, and ʿĀṣim read it heavy [خُشُب]. Whoever reads it heavy, it is as if he pluralised خشبة as خِشاب and then pluralised that again [199/b] and so made it heavy, just as they said: ثمار and ثُمُر. And if you wish, you may pluralise it — it being خشبة — as خُشُب, and make it light or heavy, just as they said: البدَنة, البُدُن and البُدْن, and الأَكَم and الأُكُم.
The Arabs pluralise some words having the form of خشبة, I think, on the pattern fuʿl; among them: أجمة and أُجْم, بَدَنة and بُدْن, أكَمة and أُكْم.
And of this kind among the weak (muʿtall) words: ساحة and سُوح, ساق and سُوق, عانة and عُون, لابة and لُوب, قارة and قور, and حياة and حِيّ. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
* ولو ترى إذ الحياة حِىّ *
(If only you had seen when life was [full of] living things.)
It should have been حُوِيّ, but its first letter was given kasra so that the ياء would not change into a واو, just as they said: بِيض and عِين.
His saying: ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Out of cowardice and fear. Then He said: "هم العدو" and did not say: هم الأعداء; and all of that is correct.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوَّوْاْ رُءُوسَهُمْ﴾.
They moved them in mockery of the Prophet ﷺ and his call. Some of the people of Medina read: "لَوَوْا رءوسهم" without doubling.

farraa:7-8.t:
His saying: ﴿هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لاَ تُنفِقُواْ عَلَىٰ مَنْ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
The Prophet ﷺ was on one of his campaigns, and a man of the Muslims called Jiʿāl and another of the hypocrites met at a watering place and jostled each other over it; Jiʿāl struck him. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy saw it and became angry, and said: We only brought these people into our home to be struck — what is the matter with them? May Allah leave them to Jiʿāl and Jiʿāl's kind! Then he said: You — if only you had withheld food from the companions of this man, they would have dispersed from him and broken away. That is His saying: ﴿هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لاَ تُنفِقُواْ عَلَىٰ مَنْ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ حَتَّىٰ يَنفَضُّواْ﴾. Then ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy said: ﴿لَئِن رَّجَعْنَآ إِلَى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ ٱلأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا ٱلأَذَلَّ﴾. Zayd ibn Arqam heard it and told the Prophet ﷺ, and the Qurʾān came down: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ ٱلْعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
It is permissible in reading: "لَيُخْرَجَنَّ الأعزُّ منها الأذلَّ", as if you said: the mighty one will surely be driven out of it humiliated [i.e. الأذلّ as ḥāl (circumstantial)]. Some read: لنُخْرِجَن الأعزَّ منها الأذل, i.e.: we will surely drive out the one who is mighty in his own estimation, humiliated.
[Translator's note: «إنكم لم منعتم» is as printed; it is understood as «إنكم لو منعتم» ("if only you had withheld").]

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The clause «قالوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause «إنك لرسول الله» is the answer to the oath, because «شهد» is treated like an oath, and for that reason it was answered with what an oath is answered with, in his words «إنك لرسول الله»; the hamza of «إن» takes kasra because of the lām in the khabar (predicate); the clause «والله يعلم إنك لرسوله» is a parenthetical clause between his words «نشهد إنك لرسول الله» and his words «والله يشهد». The clause «إنك لرسوله» stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; the clause «والله يشهد» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the apodosis «قالوا»; and the clause «إن المنافقين لكاذبون» is the answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «فصدُّوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause «اتخذوا»; the clause «إنهم ساء» is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of «ساء», which is treated like «بئس»; the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: hypocrisy (النفاق).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the khabar (predicate) of «ذلك»; the clause «فطبع» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كفروا»; and the clause «فهم لا يفقهون» is conjoined to the clause «طبع».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {اتَّخَذُوا}, and the second conditional clause is conjoined to the first conditional clause; the clause «كأنهم خشب» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: they are as if they were timbers (هم كأنهم خشب); the clause «يحسبون» is a second khabar of the implied mubtadaʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «حسب». The clause «هم العدو» is resumptive; the clause «فاحذرهم» is conjoined to the clause «هم العدو»; the clause «قاتلهم الله» is resumptive; «أنى» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause «يؤفكون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding conditional clause; the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قيل», and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «قيل»; «تعالوا»: an inflexible (jāmid) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «يستغفر» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; the clause «لَوَّوا» is the apodosis; the clause «يصدُّون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the hāʾ in «رأيتهم»; and the clause «وهم مستكبرون» is a ḥāl clause from the wāw in «يصدون».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «سواء» is a fronted khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (سواء); his words «أستغفرت»: equivalent in interpretation to a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: your asking forgiveness and its absence are alike; «أم» is a conjunction; the clause «لن يغفر الله» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «حتى ينفضُّوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تنفقوا»; the clause «ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause «ولله خزائن».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The lām is the one preparing for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); the clause «ليخرِجَنَّ» is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, the answer to the oath indicating it; the clause «ولله العزة» is resumptive; the clause «ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause «لله العزة».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «لا تُلْهكم», the answer to the vocative, is resumptive; the conditional clause is resumptive; «هم» is the separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «ممَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنفقوا»; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يأتي» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «فيقول» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يأتي»; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and the clause of urging, the answer to the vocative, is resumptive; the vocative clause and what follows it are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the fāʾ in «فأصَّدَّق» is causal (sababiyya), and the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e.: will there be a delay, and then giving of charity? His words «وأكن»: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by conjunction to the position of «فأصدق», because the implied form is: if you delay me, I will give charity and be (إن أخَّرْتني أصَّدَّقْ وأكنْ).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «ولن يؤخر الله» is resumptive; «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «بما» is attached to «خبير».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, إِذا جَاءَك المُنَافِقُونَ: the governing word in إذا is جاءك, because it contains the sense of a condition; its reason has preceded.
His saying يعلم إِنَّك لرَسُوله: إنّ has a kasra because of the entry of the lām into its khabar (predicate); so the verb is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing in the wording, while it governs in meaning the clause as a whole. Only the verbs that put the mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the accusative are suspended from governing. [Translator's note: the edition prints «عَالم» ("knowing"), apparently for عامل ("governing").]

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying إِنَّهُم سَاءَ مَا كَانُوا يعْملُونَ: ما is in the position of the nominative by ساء, according to the doctrine of Sībawayh, and كانوا يعملون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, with the هاء omitted, i.e. يعملونه. Al-Akhfash said ما is an indefinite in the position of the accusative, and كانوا يعملون is its naʿt (adjective), the هاء also being omitted from the adjective; omitting it from the ṣila is better, and it is permissible from the adjective. Ibn Kaysān said ما with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the nominative by ساء, so on his view there is no need for an omitted هاء.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying وَإِذا قيل لَهُم تَعَالَوْا يسْتَغْفر لكم: these are two verbs, of which the second, namely يستغفر, has been made to govern; there is no pronoun in it, because its fāʿil (agent) [رسول الله] comes after it. Had the first, namely تعالوا, been made to govern, in ordinary speech it would have been said تعالوا يستغفر لكم إلى رسول الله, because its implied form is "come to the Messenger of Allah, he will ask forgiveness for you" (تعالوا إلى رسول الله يستغفر لكم); so on this assumption there would be the agent pronoun in يستغفر.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying لن يغْفر الله لَهُم: لن is the particle that puts the verb in the accusative, according to Sībawayh. Al-Khalīl said its origin is لا أن; the hamza was omitted because of frequent use, then the alif was omitted because it was quiescent and the nūn was quiescent, so لن remained. لن is set up for negating the future: when you say لن يقوم زيد, it is only a negation for one who said سيقوم زيد ("Zayd will stand"); for that reason the entry of the سين and سوف with لن is not permissible, because it enters upon a future, so there is no need for the سين and سوف with it. So [in its origin] أن is what puts the verb in the accusative according to al-Khalīl.
Sībawayh held al-Khalīl to the consequence that زيدا لن أضرب ("Zayd, I will not strike") would not be permissible, because it would be within the ṣila of أن on al-Khalīl's view — and that is permissible according to both of them. Some grammarians — namely ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān [al-Akhfash the Younger] — disallowed زيدا لن أضرب on the ground that لن is not inflected (lā tanṣarif), so it is weak, and what comes after it does not come before it, just as the noun of إنّ is not permitted to come before it; and the governors of nouns are stronger than the governors of verbs, so if what comes after the governors of nouns does not come before them, while they are stronger than the governors of verbs, that is even more remote in the governors of verbs. Likewise لم, according to him. The Basrans hold that it is permissible with لن.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying ليخرجن الْأَعَز مِنْهَا الْأَذَل: this is the [normal] form of the speech, because the verb is transitive to an object, since it is from أخرج. As for whoever reads ليَخرُجن with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, the verb is intransitive, from خرج; but he puts الأذل in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the ḥāl does not have the alif and lām except in rare cases that are heard and not taken as a model for analogy. Sībawayh related ادخلوا الأولَ فالأولَ ("enter, the first then the first"), putting it in the accusative as a ḥāl, and Yūnus permitted مررت به المسكينَ ("I passed by him, the poor fellow"), putting المسكين in the accusative as a ḥāl. No analogy is made on this, because of its anomaly and its departure from the analogical rule.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying فَأَصدق وأكن: whoever omits the wāw [وأكنْ] conjoins it to the position of the فاء [clause], because its position is jussive as the answer to the wish; whoever keeps the wāw [وأكونَ] conjoins it to the wording of فأصدق. The accusative in فأصدق is by an implied أن.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله﴾: إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) of future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis; the clause جاءك is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) through the adverb's being annexed to it; المنافقون is the fāʿil (agent) of جاءك; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and it is what governs the adverb; the clause نشهد is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its noun (ism); the hamza of إن takes kasra because the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) enters upon its khabar (predicate); and رسول الله is the khabar of إن.
﴿والله يعلم﴾: the wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya). الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause ﴿يعلم﴾ is the khabar.
﴿إنك لرسوله﴾: إن is an abrogating particle, and the kāf is its noun. The lām is the shifted lām, and رسوله is the khabar of إن. ﴿إن﴾ and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of يعلم; the hamza of ﴿إن﴾ takes kasra only because the shifted lām occurs, entering upon the khabar, and the shifted lām does not occur in the khabar of ﴿أن﴾ with fatḥa on the hamza. The clause ﴿والله يعلم...﴾ is parenthetical between their saying ﴿نشهد إنك لرسول الله﴾ and His saying ﴿والله يشهد﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون﴾: الله is the mubtadaʾ, and the clause يشهد is the khabar; إن is an abrogating particle; المنافقين is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; and كاذبون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة﴾: اتخذوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); أيمانهم is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is the plural of يمين (oath); جنة is the second mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فصدوا عن سبيل الله﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; صدوا is a verb and its fāʿil; and عن سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿صدوا﴾.
﴿إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism), and the clause ساء is the khabar (predicate); ما is the fāʿil of ساء; the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the group is its noun, and the clause يعملون is the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ذلك بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition; أن together with what it enters upon is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ; and the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar (predicate) of ذلك, i.e. "because of their believing and then their disbelieving".
﴿فطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; طبع is a past verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو); على قلوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿طبع﴾; the fāʾ is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause لا يفقهون is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وإذا رأيتهم تعجبك أجسامهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) of future time; the clause رأيتهم is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) through the adverb's being annexed to it; the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis, which is تعجبك; and the clause تعجبك أجسامهم has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
﴿وإن يقولوا تسمع لقولهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; يقولوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); تسمع is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); لقولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تسمع﴾; and تسمع must be taken to include the sense of "lend an ear" and "incline", to justify its taking an object through the lām.
﴿كأنهم خشب مسندة﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in قولهم; كأن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿هم﴾ is its noun (ism), and خشب is its khabar; and مسندة is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿خشب﴾.
﴿يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم﴾: the clause is also resumptive, with no grammatical position; يحسبون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; كل صيحة is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يحسبون﴾.
﴿هم العدو﴾: هم is the mubtadaʾ and العدو the khabar; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فاحذرهم﴾: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); then an imperative verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, and a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿قاتلهم الله﴾: قاتلهم is a verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and الله is the fāʿil.
﴿أنى﴾: an interrogative noun in the place of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl.
﴿يؤفكون﴾: an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا يستغفر لكم رسول الله لووا رءوسهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb (ẓarf); the clause قيل is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) through annexation [of the adverb] to it; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قيل﴾; تعالوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); يستغفر is the answer to the command, jussive (majzūm) by the sukūn; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستغفر﴾; رسول الله is the fāʿil; لووا is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; رؤوسهم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of إذا.
﴿ورأيتهم يصدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; رأيتهم is a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, the seeing being visual; and the clause يصدون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in رأيتهم.
﴿وهم مستكبرون﴾: the clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in ﴿يصدون﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿سواء عليهم أستغفرت لهم أم لم تستغفر لهم﴾: سواء is a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿عليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سواء﴾; the hamza is for equalisation (taswiya), and together with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the interrogative hamza has made the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) unnecessary; i.e. "your seeking forgiveness and its absence are equal"; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿استغفرت﴾; أم is the counterpart (al-muʿādila) of the hamza of equalisation; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; تستغفر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾; and لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تستغفر﴾.
﴿لن يغفر الله لهم﴾: لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; يغفر is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿لن﴾; الله is the fāʿil (agent); and لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يغفر﴾.
﴿إن الله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is its noun (ism), and the clause لا يهدي is its khabar; القوم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and الفاسقين is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿هم الذين يقولون﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position, functioning as a justification of their transgression; هم is the mubtadaʾ (subject); الذين is the khabar (predicate); and the clause يقولون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله حتى ينفضوا﴾: لا is the prohibitive lā; تنفقوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); على من is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تنفقوا﴾; the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to an omitted ṣila of ﴿من﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. رسول الله is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); حتى is a particle of cause (taʿlīl) and accusative; ينفضوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تنفقوا.
﴿ولله خزائن السماوات والأرض﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لله is a fronted khabar; خزائن السماوات والأرض is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون﴾: لكن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing rectification (istidrāk); المنافقين is its noun (ism); and the clause لا يفقهون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل﴾: speech conjoined in meaning to the يقولون before it; يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the lām is the lām that prepares for an oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن is conditional; رجعنا is a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); إلى المدينة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رجعنا﴾; the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; يخرجن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, necessarily; الأعز is its fāʿil and الأذل its object; and منها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يخرجن﴾.
﴿ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); in لله, the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a fronted khabar (predicate); العزة is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and لرسوله is conjoined to لله.
﴿ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لكن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing rectification (istidrāk); المنافقين is its noun (ism); and the clause لا يعلمون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله﴾: لا is prohibitive; تلهكم is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; أموالكم is the fāʿil (agent); لا أولادكم is conjoined to أموالكم; and عن ذكر الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تلهكم﴾.
﴿ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); ذلك is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a second mubtadaʾ, or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); الخاسرون is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, and that clause is the khabar of أولئك; the clause فأولئك is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of من.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أنفقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); مما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنفقوا﴾, and من is partitive (tabʿīḍiyya); the clause ﴿رزقناكم﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من قبل is a ḥāl (circumstantial); أن together with what falls in its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, genitive (majrūr) by annexation; أحدكم is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and الموت is a postponed fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿فيقول رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive and causal (sababiyya); يقول is an imperfect verb conjoined to أن يأتي, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring back to أحدكم; لولا is for urging (taḥḍīḍiyya), meaning "why not" (هلا); أخرتني is a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, but it has the sense of the imperfect, because the لولا of urging is particular to the past verb interpreted as imperfect; the tāʾ is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إلى أجل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخرتني﴾; and قريب is a naʿt (adjective). ﴿فأصدق﴾: the fāʾ is causal; أصدق is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal fāʾ; the fāʾ and what follows it are in the position of a jussive (majzūm), because it is the answer to the urging; the interpreted maṣdar from أن أصدق is conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the supplication embodied in the urging, i.e. "is there to be a postponement of the term, and so [my] giving charity?"; ﴿أكن﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive by conjunction with the position of ﴿فأصدق﴾; the noun (ism) of ﴿أكن﴾ is latent, its implied form being "I" (أنا); and ﴿من الصالحين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿أكن﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿ولن يؤخر الله نفسا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to something supplied; لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; يؤخر is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿لن﴾; الله is the fāʿil (agent); and نفسًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إذا جاء أجلها﴾: إذا is a future adverb (ẓarf) that includes the sense of condition; the clause جاء أجلها is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) through the adverb's being annexed to it; and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
﴿والله خبير بما تعملون﴾: الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject); خبير is the khabar (predicate); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خبير﴾; and the clause تعملون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
That is: let it not bring about distraction (al-lahw) in you, as though it were from «ألهيتُه فلها» (I distracted him, and he became distracted), as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 488-
ومثلك حبلى قد طرقت ومرضع ... فألهيتها عن ذي تمائم محول
(Many a one like you, pregnant, have I visited by night, and many a nursing mother, and I distracted her from her year-old infant wearing amulets.)
وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ: that is, those who are cheated of mercy and reward.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
وَأَنْفِقُوا مِنْ ما رَزَقْناكُمْ: it has been said that this indicates that one does not say "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, provided him with it" except of what is lawful. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلا أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ: an answer (jawāb). وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the position (mawḍiʿ) of the fāʾ, not to what comes after the fāʾ. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū ʿAmr read «وأكونَ» (وأكون) in the accusative (naṣb), conjoining it to what comes after the fāʾ. It has been reported that this is how it is in the reading of Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd: «وأكونَ» (وأكون); however, it contradicts the written text of the codex (al-sawād) by which the proof has been established. Some of them argued for it, saying: the wāw is dropped in such cases, just as one says «كلمن» and it is written without a wāw.
It is reported that Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] countered this view, the evidence that it is not sound being that the writing of the codex in parallel cases is otherwise, such as يكون, تكون and نكون, all written with the wāw in the nominative and accusative positions alike, and nothing else is permissible. Someone else said: the case of «كلمن» is different from this, because the wāw was only dropped from it since they wanted to show that the form of the wāw was connected; so since it had already come in «هوّز» they did not need to repeat it; likewise they did not write it in their saying «أبجد». As for ordinary speech, none of this is permissible. Nor is there any need for it, because conjunction to the position (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-mawḍiʿ) is found frequently in the speech of the Arabs. Sībawayh said: had the fāʾ not been there, it would have been jussive (majzūm), meaning: because it is the answer to the interrogative that carries the sense of a wish (tamannī). As the poet said — someone other than Sībawayh recited it: [al-Wāfir] 489-
فأبلوني بليّتكم لعلّي ... أصالحكم وأستدرج نويّا
(So grant me your favour, that perhaps I may make peace with you and draw my journey back.)
And Sībawayh recited, concerning conjunction to the position: [al-Ṭawīl] 490-
فإن لم تجد من دون عدنان والدا ... ودون معدّ فلتزعك العواذل
(If you find no father below ʿAdnān, nor below Maʿadd, then let the blamers restrain you.)
Because the meaning of «من دون عدنان» is «دون عدنان». And he recited: [al-Wāfir] 491-
معاوي إنّنا بشر فأسجح ... فلسنا بالجبال ولا الحديدا
(Muʿāwiya, we are human beings, so be gentle; we are not mountains, nor iron.)
] And likewise his saying: [al-Kāmil] 492-
لا أمّ لي إن كان ذاك ولا أب
(Let me have no mother, if that is so, and no father.)
And likewise his saying: [al-Sarīʿ] 493-
لا نسب اليوم ولا خلّة ... اتّسع الخرق على الرّاقع
(No kinship today and no friendship; the rent has grown too wide for the patcher.)
— conjoined to the position; if you bring it according to the wording you say «ولا خلةً». Similar to it from the Qur'an is مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرُهُمْ [al-Aʿrāf: 186], conjoined to the position of the fāʾ, and with the nominative conjoined to what comes after the fāʾ. The origin of فأصّدّق is «فأتصدّق»: the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād, and this was good because they are in one word and because they are close to each other. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: «فأصّدّق» "and I would give alms (and purify myself)" and وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ "I would perform the Hajj". Someone else said: "I would be among the righteous" means "I would perform the obligatory duties and avoid the forbidden things". The implied form is: "and I would be righteous, one of the righteous".

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
وَلَنْ يُؤَخِّرَ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِذا جاءَ أَجَلُها: accusative (manṣūb) by «لن» according to Sībawayh. According to al-Khalīl, its origin is «لا أن», and it is reported from him that no verb is put in the accusative except by «أن», whether implied or overt. Sībawayh refuted that on the grounds that one may say:
«زيدا لن أضرب» (Zayd I will not strike), but one may not say «زيدا يعجبني أن تضرب» (Zayd it pleases me that you strike), because [Zayd] is inside the ṣila (relative clause) and so cannot precede.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: In my view, «زيدا لن أضرب» is not permissible, because «لن» is not inflectable (lā yataṣarraf), so nothing connected with what it governs may precede it, just as «زيدا إنّ عمرا يضرب» is not permissible; and «لم» is likewise in his view. I related this to Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] and he rejected it, saying: no one has said this. Abū ʿUbayda claimed that some of the Arabs make the jussive with «لن», but this is not known. يُؤَخِّرَ is with hamza, because its origin is from «أخّر», and the hamza is written as a wāw even though it has fatḥa, for two reasons. One of them is that before it is a ḍamma, and the ḍamma prevails because of its strength. The other is that it may not be written as an alif, because what precedes an alif can only be with fatḥa. Whoever lightens the hamza turns it into a wāw and says «يؤخّر». If it is asked: why is it not made "between-between" (bayna bayna)?
The answer is that if it were made between-between, it would be inclined towards the alif, and that would be an error, because what precedes an alif can only be with fatḥa. إِذا جاءَ أَجَلُها: with both hamzas fully pronounced; if you wish you may lighten [one]. Abū ʿAmr drops [one] because [the other] indicates it, since their vowels are the same and the hamza stands on its own. وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ: that is, possessed of full awareness of your deeds, so He records them against you and will requite you for them. The order of speech is that the preposition and its genitive noun should come at the end, because they are an explanation (tabyīn); if any of that comes first, it is intended to be at the end. For this reason the grammarians agreed that one may not say «لبستُ ألينها من الثياب» (I wore the softest of them, of the garments), because the preposition and its genitive noun are at the end in their proper place, so they cannot be intended as coming first. The correct form of the example is «لبس من الثياب ألينها». If you take «ما» to mean «الذي» (which), then the hāʾ is omitted, i.e. «خبير بما تعملونه» (aware of what you do it); it was omitted because of the length of the noun. If you take «ما» as maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), you need no omission, i.e. "and Allah is possessed of full awareness of your doing".

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: إِذا is in the position of an accusative by جاءك, except that it is not declined, because of its shifting [reference] and because at its end there is an alif, and the alif takes no vowel. The response to إذا is قالُوا نَشْهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ: «إن» is given kasra because of the entry of the lām; and the speech was cut off, so إنّ came at the start and was given kasra. وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لَكاذِبُونَ: the name of Allah the Exalted is repeated overtly because that is more majestic. It is said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, gave them the lie regarding what they concealed. Among the soundest of what has been said about it is that they declared that their own selves firmly held faith while they were lying, so Allah gave them the lie.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ جُنَّةً: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is their swearing by Allah that they are indeed of you; and Qatāda said: a shield, by which they protect their blood and their property. Al-Ḥasan read اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ [Translator's note: i.e. إِيمانَهُمْ, "their faith", with kasra; the print shows the standard vowelling], i.e. their profession of belief, as a covering with which they cover themselves just as one covers oneself with a shield in war; so killing them and taking their offspring captive was prevented, because they displayed faith. فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: the object may be omitted, i.e. they turned people away; and the verb may be intransitive, i.e. they turned away from the way of Allah, i.e. His religion with which He is pleased and His law with which He sent His Prophet ﷺ. إِنَّهُمْ ساءَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ: of their swearing to lies and their hypocrisy. «ما» is in the position of a nominative according to the view of Sībawayh, i.e. "evil is the thing", and in the position of an accusative according to the view of al-Akhfash, i.e. "evil is it as a thing which they do".

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: ذلِكَ is in the position of a nominative, i.e. that swearing and hypocrisy is because they آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا فطبع على قلوبهم. Assimilating the ʿayn into the ʿayn is permissible, and not assimilating is better because of the remoteness of the ʿayn's place of articulation. فَهُمْ لا يَفْقَهُونَ truth from falsehood nor right from wrong, because of desire's dominance over them.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَإِذا رَأَيْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ أَجْسامُهُمْ: all the grammarians permitted the jussive by إذا and that it be treated as one of the particles of requital (conditional particles), because it only occurs with a verb and needs a response, and so it is with the particles of requital. Al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Kāmil] 484-
واستغن ما أغناك ربّك بالغنى ... وإذا تصبك خصاصة فتجمّل
(Be content with wealth as long as your Lord enriches you, and when need befalls you, bear it with dignity)
 And another recited: [al-Basīṭ] 485-
نارا إذا ما خبت نيرانهم تقد
(A fire that blazes whenever their fires die down)
 The preference according to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ is not to use the jussive with إذا, because what comes after it is timed (muwaqqat), so it differs from the particles of requital in this, as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 486-
وإذا تكون شديدة أدعى لها ... وإذا يحاس الحيس يدعى جندب
(When there is a hardship, I am called for it; and when the ḥays is being mixed, Jundab is called)
 وَإِنْ يَقُولُوا تَسْمَعْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ, because their speech is like the speech of the people of faith. كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ i.e. they do not understand, and they have no understanding or knowledge, so they are like timber. This [khushubun] is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza; and Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read خشب with the shīn quiescent [khushbun], and Abū ʿUbayd inclines to it, claiming that he does not know faʿala [Translator's note: i.e. faʿala-t, the singular خَشَبة] being pluralized on fuʿul with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the ʿayn. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake and an attack on what the multitude has transmitted. That is not free from one of two aspects: either خشب [khashab] is the plural of خشبة, as in their saying ثمرة and ثمر, so it would be other than what he said about faʿala being pluralized on fuʿul; or it is as the skilled grammarians said: خشبة and خشاب, like جفنة and جفان, and خشاب and خشب [khushub], like حمار and حمر. Moreover, أكمة, أكم and أكم, and أجمة and أجم have been heard. As for خشب [khushb], its original may be khushub, with the ḍamma dropped because of its heaviness; and it may be — and this is better — like أسد and أسد [usd] in the masculine. Sībawayh said: and like خشبة and خشب is بدنة and بدن, and like it in the masculine وثن and وثن [wuthn]. He said: and it is a reading. I reckon that whoever interpreted Sībawayh['s words] "and it is a reading" to mean «كأنّهم خشب» [is mistaken], because his saying "and it is a reading" is a weakening of it; rather, as is said, he means: «إن تدعون من دونه إلّا وثنا» [Translator's note: i.e. وُثُناً], and this is an anomalous reading narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās. يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ i.e. because of their cowardice and the paucity of their certainty, and because they conceal disbelief: whenever revelation came down they were alarmed lest they had been exposed. هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ, because their tongues are with you and their hearts with the disbelievers, so they are spies for them; and عدو has the meaning of أعداء (enemies). فَاحْذَرْهُمْ قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ i.e. He punished them and destroyed them, so they became like one who has been killed. أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ i.e. from where are they turned away from the truth after the proofs have become manifest?

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعالَوْا يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: this is on the basis of giving governing effect to the second verb, just as you say:
أقبل يكلمك زيد; if you gave governing effect to the first you would say أقبل يكلمك إلى زيد, and تعالوا يستغفر لكم إلى رسول الله. لَوَّوْا رُؤُسَهُمْ [Translator's note: i.e. لَوَوْا, without doubling, as the following contrast requires] may be for a small number, and لوّوا for multiplicity. وَرَأَيْتَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ i.e. turning away from going to the Prophet ﷺ so that he might seek forgiveness for them.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ is nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ is in the position of the khabar (predicate), and the meaning is: seeking forgiveness and not doing so. لَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ, because they are disbelievers. The Prophet ﷺ only sought forgiveness for them because outwardly they were Muslims, so the meaning of his seeking forgiveness for them was: "O Allah, forgive them if they are believers." إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ: it is said: i.e. He does not grant them success; and it is said: He does not guide them to the reward and Paradise.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: يَنْفَضُّوا i.e. they disperse. Qatāda said: the one who said this was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy; he said: "Were it not that you spend on them, they would leave him and abandon him." Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: «هم» refers to them and to whoever held his view. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is better than the view of whoever said that «هم» refers to one person. وَلِلَّهِ خَزائِنُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ i.e. in His hand are the keys of the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, so no one gives anyone anything except by His permission, nor withholds it except by His will. وَلكِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لا يَفْقَهُونَ that this is so; and for this reason they say: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
