يَقُولُونَ لَئِنْ رَجَعْنا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ: al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ related that it is read لنخرجنّ الأعزّ منها الأذلّ with the nūn, and that this means "we shall surely drive out the mighty from it, abased" [Translator's note: i.e. with الأذلَّ as a ḥāl]. Al-Farrāʾ related: ليخرجنّ الأعزّ منها الأذلّ [Translator's note: i.e. layakhrujanna, "the mightier will surely go out from it, abased"], also in the meaning of "abased" (dhalīlan). Most grammarians do not permit the ḥāl to have the alif and lām, except that Yūnus permitted مررت به المسكين, and Sībawayh related دخلوا الأوّل فالأوّل; but these are things on which the Qurʾān may not be construed — except that ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: «ليخرجنّ» may operate like لتكونن, so that its khabar is definite. الأعز and العزيز are one, i.e. the strong, the secure, the unassailable, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 487-
إذا ابتدر القوم السّلاح وجدتني ... عزيزا إذا بلّت بقائمة يدي
(When the people rush to their weapons, you find me mighty once my hand has gripped the hilt)
 It is also narrated «منيعا», and the meaning is the same. وَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلكِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ i.e. and so they said this.

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is the lām of oath, which substitutes for the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) because of the sense of oath in (نشهد); this is in the first and third places, while it is the shifted lām in the second place. (الواو) is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and the second is a conjunction.
The clause «جاءك المنافقون ... » is in the position of a genitive muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «نشهد ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «إنّك لرسول اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath «1».
The clause «اللَّه يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
The clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللَّه).
The clause «إنّك لرسوله ... » is in the position of an accusative, filling the place of the two objects of يعلم [Note: the hamza of (إنّ) is given kasra because of the lām coming in the khabar.].
The clause «اللَّه يشهد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the apodosis of the condition.
The clause «يشهد ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللَّه).
The clause «إنّ المنافقين لكاذبون» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath «3».
2- (جنّة) is an accusative second direct object. (عن سبيل) is attached to (صدّوا). (ساء) is a past verb for forming censure (inshāʾ al-dhamm). (ما) is an indefinite described noun, the agent [Note: or a relative noun - in the position of a nominative -[.....] and the specified object of censure is omitted, its implied form being "hypocrisy" - or "lack of steadfastness in faith" - The clause «اتّخذوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «صدّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اتّخذوا.
The clause «إنّهم ساء ما كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ساء ما كانوا ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of inna.
The clause «كانوا يعملون» is in the position of a nominative naʿt of (ما) [Note: or it has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun ما.].
The clause «يعملون» is in the position of an accusative khabar of كانوا. 3- The demonstrative in (ذلك) refers to the evil of their deed. (على قلوبهم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (الفاء) is causal. (لا) is a negation.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم آمنوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «آمنوا ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of anna.
The clause «كفروا ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
The clause «طبع على قلوبهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause.
The clause «هم لا يفقهون» has no grammatical position; it is causal [Note: the clause may be a consequence of the sealing of their hearts, in which case it is conjoined to the clause طبع على قلوبهم.].
The clause «لا يفقهون» is in the position of a nominative khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
4- (الواو) is a conjunction in the two places. (لقولهم) is attached to (تسمع). (عليهم) is attached to an omitted second direct object. (الفاء) is a conjunction linking the effect to the cause. (أنّى) is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative adverb of place, attached to a ḥāl from the wāw in (يؤفكون).
The clause «رأيتهم ... » is in the position of a genitive muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تعجبك أجسامهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يقولوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumption formed of the condition, its protasis and its apodosis.
The clause «تسمع ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the condition, not joined by fāʾ.
The clause «كأنّهم خشب ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun in قولهم.].
The clause «يحسبون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «هم العدوّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «احذرهم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "be aware of this, and beware of them."
The clause «قاتلهم اللَّه» has no grammatical position; it is a resumptive supplication.
The clause «يؤفكون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
5- (الواو) is a conjunction in the two places, and a ḥāl wāw in the third. (لهم) is attached to (قيل). (يستغفر) is a jussive imperfect verb, the response to the imperative. (لوّوا) is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns.
The clause «قيل ... » is in the position of a genitive muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تعالوا ... » is in the position of a nominative nāʾib fāʿil [Note: it is originally the content of the saying for the active verb.].
The clause «يستغفر لكم رسول ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position, not joined by fāʾ, i.e.: "if you accept, he will ask forgiveness."
The clause «لوّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition (إذا).
The clause «رأيتهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لوّوا.
The clause «يصدّون ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (رأيتهم).
The clause «هم مستكبرون» is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يصدّون.

* Morphology:
(4) خشب: it is said to be a collective noun (ism jamʿ) whose singular is خشبة with two fatḥas or with a fatḥa and a sukūn; and it is said to be a plural of خشب with two fatḥas, like أسد and أسد; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas.
(مسنّدة) is the feminine of مسنّد, a passive participle from the quadriliteral (سنّد); its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(5) لوّوا: it has an elision (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf): the lām of the word was dropped because of its meeting, as a sukūn, with the plural wāw; its pattern is فعّوا.

* Rhetoric:
The unrestricted representative simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal al-tamthīlī) in the words of Allah the Exalted «كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ».
They were likened, in sitting in the gatherings of the Messenger ﷺ, leaning in them, while they are only bodies empty of faith and goodness, to timbers set up and leaned against a wall, in being forms empty of benefit; for timbers are leaned when they are not in a building or propped by something else. It is also possible that what is meant by the leaned timbers is the idols carved from wood and leaned against walls. They were likened to them in the beauty of their forms and the scarcity of their usefulness.
The point of resemblance is that both sides are shapes empty of knowledge and perception.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(سواء) is a preposed khabar, nominative. (عليهم) is attached to (سواء), and the (الهمزة) is for equalization (taswiya) and is a maṣdar particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (أستغفرت لهم) is in the position of a nominative postposed mubtadaʾ.
(لهم) is attached to (استغفرت). (أم) is a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction. The second (لهم) is attached to (تستغفر), and the third (لهم) is attached to (يغفر). (لا) is a negation..
The clause «سواء عليهم (استغفارك) ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «استغفرت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative.
The clause «لم تستغفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause استغفرت.
The clause «لن يغفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «إنّ اللَّه لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of inna.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle. (على من) is attached to the prohibited (تنفقوا). (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative من. (حتّى) is a particle of limit and genitive. (ينفضّوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after حتّى..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ينفضّوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive by (حتّى), attached to (تنفقوا).
(الواو) is a ḥāl wāw. (للَّه) is attached to the preposed khabar of the mubtadaʾ خزائن. (لا) is a negation.
The clause «هم الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تنفقوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «ينفضّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «للَّه خزائن ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl [Note: or resumptive.].
The clause «لكنّ المنافقين لا يفقهون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the resumptive.].
The clause «لا يفقهون ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of لكنّ.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is the preparatory lām for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa lil-qasam). (إن) is a jussive conditional particle. (رجعنا) is an indeclinable past verb in the position of the jussive, being the protasis. (إلى المدينة) is attached to (رجعنا). (اللام) is the lām of oath. (منها) is attached to (يخرجنّ). (الواو) is a ḥāl wāw. (للَّه العزّة) is like للَّه خزائن «1». (ولكنّ المنافقين لا يعلمون) is like ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون, in words and clauses «2». The clause «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إن رجعنا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «يخرجن الأعزّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath. The apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.

* Morphology:
(الأذلّ) is an elative (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral ذلّ; its pattern is أفعل, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.

* Rhetoric:
The art of "saying with the necessary implication" (fann al-qawl bi-l-mūjib): in the words of Allah the Exalted يَقُولُونَ لَئِنْ رَجَعْنا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ.
This art is that the speaker addresses a person with a statement, and this addressed person goes to each single word of the speaker's statement and builds upon it, from his own speech, something that necessitates the reverse of the speaker's meaning; for the reality of "saying with the necessary implication" is the opponent's rebuttal of his adversary's statement from the very import of that statement. The necessary implication of the hypocrites' statement mentioned above in the verse is the Messenger's expelling the hypocrites from Medina, and that did happen. Do you not see that Allah the Exalted said right after it: «واللَّه العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون»?

* Benefits:
The abasement of the hypocrites..
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, and two men pushed each other, one an Anṣārī and one a Muhājir, and each called to his companions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked into the matter and said: "Leave it, for it is foul; it is from the call of the Jāhiliyya." The news reached ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, the head of hypocrisy, and he said: "Have they done it (meaning the Muhājirūn)? By Allah, if we return to Medina, the mightier of us (meaning himself) will surely expel the more abased (meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ)." The news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and ʿUmar said: "Permit me to strike his neck." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Would it please you that people say that Muḥammad kills his companions?" On the way back, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy lay in wait at the entrance of Medina and prevented his father from entering, saying to him: "You are the abased, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the mighty." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ learned of the news and sent word to ʿAbd Allāh to allow his father to enter. The son said:
"If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permits, then yes."

safi-cedvel:9-11.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) is an indefinite specified vocative, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of an accusative badal from أيّ - or ʿaṭf bayān on it. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle. (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis of the prohibition. (أولادكم) is conjoined to أموالكم and nominative. (عن ذكر) is attached to (تلهكم). (الواو) is resumptive. (من) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ. (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis. (هم) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الخاسرون.. and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.].
The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تلهكم أموالكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «من يفعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يفعل ذلك ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: or the khabar is the two clauses of condition and apodosis together.].
The clause «أولئك.. الخاسرون» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of the condition, joined by fāʾ.
10- (الواو) is a conjunction. (ممّا) is attached to (أنفقوا), and the returning pronoun is omitted. (من قبل) is attached to (أنفقوا). (أن) is a maṣdar and accusative particle. (الموت) is the agent of (يأتي), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the precursors of death". (الفاء) is a conjunction. (يقول) is an accusative imperfect verb conjoined to يأتي..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي ... ) is in the position of a genitive muḍāf ilayhi.
(ربّ) is an accusative muḍāf vocative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ that was dropped for lightness. (لولا) is a particle of urging, with the sense of supplication. (إلى أجل) is attached to (أخّرتني). (الفاء) is the fāʾ of causation. (أصدّق) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ. (الواو) is a conjunction. (أكن) is a defective imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, conjoined to the clause of supplication [Note: or conjoined to the position of (فأصّدّق) according to the meaning.. i.e. "if You delay me, I shall give charity - jussive - and be ..."]. (من الصالحين) is attached to the khabar of أكن.
The clause «أنفقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «رزقناكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يأتي ... الموت» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «يقول ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يأتي.. الموت.
The clause «ربّ ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying [Note: or parenthetical, with the clause أخّرتني being the content of the saying.].
The clause «أخّرتني ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «أصّدّق ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أصّدّق.) is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the preceding supplication embodied in the particle of urging, i.e. "Is there a delay in the term, so that I may give zakāt?"
The clause «أكن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined by fāʾ.
11- (الواو) is resumptive and the second is a conjunction. (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause after it being its ṣila.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون..) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the khabar (خبير).
The clause «لن يؤخّر اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «جاء أجلها ... » is in the position of a genitive muḍāf ilayhi.. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "then Allah will not delay it" [Note: the adverb may be devoid of conditionality, in which case there is no apodosis, and the adverb is then attached to the mentioned verb يؤخر.].
The clause «اللَّه خبير ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يؤخّر اللَّه.
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(9) تلهكم: it has an elision (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf): its lām was dropped to match the jussive; its pattern is تفعكم [Translator's note: the source text of this entry ends here, apparently cut off mid-discussion.]

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِذَا جَآءَكَ}: a condition (sharṭ). It was said: its apodosis is «قالوا». It was also said: it is omitted. And «قالوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "they came to you saying such-and-such, so do not accept it from them." It was also said: the apodosis is {اتخذوا أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً}, which is remote, and «قالوا» is also a ḥāl.
His saying: {قَالُواْ نَشْهَدُ}: it follows the course of an oath, like a verb of knowledge and certainty, and for that reason it is met with what an oath is met with, in His saying {إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ الله}, and in his saying:
4262 - ولقد عَلِمْتُ لَتَأْتِيَنَّ مَنِيَّتي ... إنَّ المنايا لا تَطيشُ سِهامُها
(I have known that my death will surely come; the arrows of fate do not miss.)
The disagreement of the people about truthfulness and lying, their use of this verse as evidence, and the answer to it, have been given at the beginning of [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
His saying: {والله يَعْلَمُ}: a parenthetical clause between His saying {نَشْهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ} and His saying {والله يَشْهَدُ}, for a benefit. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Had He said «قالوا نشهد إنَّك لرسول الله، واللَّهُ يَشْهد إنَّهم لكاذبون», it would have suggested that this statement of theirs is a lie; so He put between the two His saying {والله يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ} to remove this ambiguity."

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {اتخذوا}: it has been given that it may be the apodosis of the condition, and it may be resumptive, brought to show their lying and their swearing to it, that is: what moved them to take oaths was their guarding themselves with them. The majority read it with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of «يمين»; al-Ḥasan read it with kasra, as a maṣdar. The like of it was given in [Sūrat] al-Mujādila. الجُنَّة is the shield and the like, and everything that protects you from harm. Among the sayings of the eloquent: «جُبَّةُ البُرْدِ جُنَّةُ البَرْدِ» (a cloak of striped cloth is a shield against the cold). Aʿshā of Hamdān said:
4263 - إذا أنتَ لم تجعلْ لِعرْضِكَ جُنَّةً ... من المالِ سار الذَّمُّ كلَّ مَسِيرِ
(If you do not make a shield of wealth for your honour, blame travels every road.)
His saying: {سَآءَ مَا كَانُواْ}: it may be the one that behaves like biʾsa, or it may be in its ordinary sense; the first is clearer, and the ruling for each has been given, and praise be to Allah. His saying «فطُبِعَ»: this is the reading of the majority, I mean its construction in the passive; and what takes the place of the agent is the preposition and its genitive noun after it. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «وطَبَعَ» in the active. There are two possibilities regarding the agent. One is that it is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, and the reading of al-Aʿmash points to this, as does his own reading in one transmission, «فَطَبَعَ اللَّهُ», with the Name stated. The second is that the agent is a pronoun referring to the maṣdar understood from what precedes, that is: "so it sealed", meaning their trifling with the religion.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {تَسْمَعْ}: the majority read it in the second person, and «لِقولهم» is attached to it; «تَسْمَعْ» was made to imply the sense of "you incline and lend an ear", and for that reason it was made transitive with the lām. It was also said that the lām is rather added (mazīda), that is, "you hear their speech". That is of no account, given the clarity of the meaning of the first. ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī and ʿIkrima read it with a yāʾ from below, in the passive, and what takes the place of the agent is the preposition and its genitive noun, because of the implication mentioned earlier. Whoever held the lām to be added in the first case is not allowed to hold it so here, that is, "you hear their speech", because the lām is not added to the agent nor to what resembles it.
His saying: {كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ}: there are three possibilities regarding this clause. The first is that it is resumptive. The second is that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "They are as though they were"; al-Zamakhsharī stated these two. The third is that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, the owner of the ḥāl being the pronoun in «قولِهم»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī and Qunbul read «خُشْب» with ḍamma and sukūn; the rest of the Seven with two ḍammas. The two Saʿīds, Ibn Jubayr and Ibn al-Musayyab, read it with two fatḥas, and al-Zamakhsharī ascribed it to Ibn ʿAbbās and mentioned no one else. As for the reading with two ḍammas, it was said that it may be a plural of خشَبَة like ثَمَرَة and ثُمُر; al-Zamakhsharī [spelled in the source "al-Zamshkhasharī"] said this, and there is room for objection, because this pattern is memorized for faʿala and is not regular, like ثَمَرَة and ثُمُر. Al-Fāsī reported from al-Zubaydī that it is a plural of خَشْباء, and I think he was mistaken about him, for he may have said «خُشْب» with sukūn as a plural of خَشْباء like حَمْراء and حُمْر, because the descriptive faʿlāʾ is not pluralized as fuʿul with two ḍammas but with ḍamma and sukūn. His saying "al-Zubaydī" is a scribal error (taṣḥīf), either his or the copyist's; it is rather al-Yazīdī, the student of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ; al-Zamakhsharī reported that. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "And «خُشْب» with ḍamma and sukūn is a plural of خَشَب, like أَسَد and أُسْد." End. This suggests that one says أُسُد with two ḍammas, and it is not so.
As for the reading with ḍamma and sukūn, it was said that it is a lightening of the first. It was also said that it is a plural of خَشْباء, which is the piece of wood whose inside has rotted, that is, been emptied; they were likened to it because their insides are empty of what is of benefit. It was also said that it is a plural of خَشَبة like بَدَنَة and بُدْن; al-Zamakhsharī said this.
As for the reading with two fatḥas, it is a generic noun (ism jins), and its qualifier was made feminine, as in His saying {نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 7], which is one of the two permissible forms.
And His saying {مُّسَنَّدَةٌ} draws attention to the fact that they are not benefited from as wood is benefited from in a roof and the like; or they were likened to idols, because they used to lean them against walls.
His saying: {يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ}: there are two possibilities. The clearer is that «عليهم» is the second object of "supposing", that is: "falling and being upon them", and His saying «هم العدوُّ» is a resumptive clause, by which Allah the Exalted informs. The second is that «عليهم» is attached to «صيحة», and the clause «هم العدوُّ» is in the position of the second object of "supposing". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that «هم العدوُّ» is the second object, as if you had cast off the pronoun. If you ask: its proper form would be to say «هي العدو»; I say: regard is had to the khabar, as was mentioned in His saying
{هذا رَبِّي} [al-Anʿām: 77], and a muḍāf may be implied: «يَحْسَبُون كلَّ أهلِ صيحةٍ»." End. The second involves great remoteness.
His saying: {أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ}: «أنَّى» is in the sense of «كيف». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that «أنَّى» is an adverbial of «قاتَلَهم», as if He said: 'May Allah fight them, how they turn away, or are turned away!' and so there would be no question in the saying on this view." End. This is not permissible, because «أنَّى» is only in the sense of «كيف», or in the sense of the conditional or interrogative «أين»; and on all three assumptions it is not purely adverbial, so what precedes it does not govern it at all, just as it does not govern in the nouns of condition and interrogation.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ الله}: the grammarians counted this question as one of iʿmāl (competing governors). That is because «تعالَوا» requires «رسولُ الله» as genitive with «إلى», that is: "come to the Messenger of Allah", while «يَسْتغفر» requires it as agent; so the second was made to govern, and for that reason it is nominative, and it was omitted from the first, the implied form being: "come to him". Had the first governed, it would have been said: «إلى رسولِ الله يَسْتغفر», with an agent latent in «يَسْتغفر». It may be said that this is not a case of iʿmāl at all, because His saying «تعالَوْا» is a command to approach as such, without regard to one approached.
His saying: {لَوَّوْا}: this is the apodosis of «إذا». Nāfiʿ read «لَوَوْا» lightened; the rest with shadda, for intensification. And «يَصُدُّون» is a ḥāl because the seeing is of the eye; and likewise His saying «وهم مُستكبرون» is also a ḥāl, either from the owner of the first ḥāl, or from the agent of «يَصُدُّون», in which case it is nested. He brought «يَصُدُّون» in the imperfect to indicate renewal and continuity. «يَصِدُّون» with kasra was also read, and it has been given in [Sūrat] al-Zukhruf.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ}: the reading of the majority is with a hamza with fatḥa without a madd, which is the hamza of equalization (hamzat al-taswiya), whose origin is the interrogative. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read «آسْتَغْفَرْت» with a hamza and then an alif, and the people differed in interpreting it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a lengthening of the interrogative hamza for display and clarity, not a conversion of the hamzat al-waṣl as in «آلسحرُ» and «آللهُ»." He means that he lengthened the fatḥa of the hamza of equalization so that an alif arose from it, his purpose in that being to show the hamza and make it clear, and not that he converted the connective into an alif as it is converted in His saying «آلسحرُ» and «آللهُ أَذِنَ لكم», because that hamza is a connective, and so it drops in continuous speech. Moreover, it has a kasra, so the question is not confused with a statement, unlike «آلسحر» and «آلله». Others said: it is a replacement for the hamzat al-waṣl, as in «آلذَّاكَرَيْن». This is of no account, because this one has a kasra, so how can it be replaced by an alif? Further, we converted it there into an alif and did not drop it, though dropping it was due, lest the question be confused with a statement; and here there is no confusion.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Abū Jaʿfar, meaning Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, read «آستغفرْتَ» with a madd on the hamza, which is the alif of equalization. He also read it with the alif joined, without a hamza, as a statement; and in all this there is weakness, because in the first he retained the hamzat al-waṣl when the interrogative hamza had made it unnecessary, and in the second he dropped the interrogative hamza while intending it, which is not used except in poetry." I say: as for his reading «استغفرْتَ» with the hamza joined, it was also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, except that he puts ḍamma on the mīm of «عليهم» when he joins the hamza, because its origin is ḍamma, whereas Abū ʿAmr puts kasra on it by the rule of the meeting of two quiescent letters. As for his saying "which is not used except in poetry": if by this he means lengthening this hamza in this place, it is correct, indeed we do not find it either; but if he means dropping the interrogative hamza, it is not correct, because dropping it is permissible by consensus before «أم», in prose and verse. As for without «أم», there is disagreement; al-Akhfash permits it and makes {وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 22] an instance of it, and the saying: 4264 - طَرِبْتُ وما شَوْقاً إلى البيضِ أَطْرَبُ ... ولا لَعِباً مني وذو الشَّيْبِ يَلْعَبُ
(I was stirred, though it is not out of longing for the fair ones that I am stirred, nor in play from me, and does one with grey hair play?)
and the saying of another:
4265 - أَفْرَحُ أَنْ أُرْزَأَ الكرامَ وأَنْ ... أُوْرَثَ ذَوْداً شصائِصاً نَبْلا
(Do I rejoice that I be bereaved of the noble, and that I inherit a few barren she-camels...?)
As for before «أم», it is frequent, as in his saying:
4266 - لَعَمْرُكَ ما أَدْري وإنْ كنتُ داريا ... بسَبْعٍ رَمَيْنَ الجَمْر أم بثمانٍ
(By your life, I do not know, though I be one who knows, whether they cast the pebbles with seven or with eight.)
This question has already been treated fully, and praise be to Allah.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {يَنفَضُّواْ}: the majority read it from الانْفِضاض, which is dispersing. Al-Faḍl ibn ʿĪsā al-Raqāshī read «يُنْفِضُوا», from أَنْفَضَ القومُ, meaning their provisions were exhausted. One says: نَفَضَ الرجلُ وعاءَه من الزاد, then أَنْفَضَ; so it is transitive without the hamza and not transitive with it, and is of the pattern كَبَبْتُه فأَكَبَّ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its reality is: the time came for them to shake out their provision bags."

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الأعز}: the reading of the majority is with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, predicated of «الأعزُّ», with «الأذلَّ» the direct object; and "the mightier" is, by his claim, some of the hypocrites. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Musayyabī read «لَنُخْرِجَنَّ» with the nūn of magnification and «الأعَزَّ» in the accusative as direct object and «الأذلّ» in the accusative as ḥāl, and those who allowed it to be made definite used this as evidence. The majority made the «أل» redundant, on the pattern of:
4267 - فَأَرْسَلَها العِراكَ. . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(So he sent them [to the water] in a crowd...)
and "enter first the first" («وادخلوا الأَوَّلَ فالأَوَّلَ»). Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be accusative as direct object, its governor being an omitted ḥāl, that is: "resembling the lowly". Al-Zamakhsharī explained it by an omitted muḍāf, that is "the going out of the lowly" or "the expelling of the lowly", meaning according to the two readings, from خَرَجَ and أَخْرَجَ; on this it is accusative as a maṣdar, not as a ḥāl. Al-Dānī reported from al-Ḥasan also «لنَخْرُجَنَّ» with fatḥa on the nūn of magnification and ḍamma on the rāʾ and «الأعزَّ» in the accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification), like their saying «نحن العربَ أَقْرى الناس للضيفِ», and «الأذلَّ» accusative as a ḥāl too; the Shaykh said this, and there is room for objection: how could they inform about themselves that they will go out in a state of lowliness while saying "the mightier", that is, "I specify the mightier", meaning by "the mightier" themselves? Abū Ḥātim also reported this reading. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported that some people read «ليَخْرُجَنَّ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the rāʾ and «الأعزُّ» nominative as agent and the first accusative as ḥāl, which is clear. «ليُخْرَجَنَّ» was also read with a yāʾ in the passive, «الأعزُّ» taking the place of the agent, «الأذلَّ» a ḥāl too.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {وَأَكُن}: Abū ʿAmr read «وأكونَ» with the verb in the accusative by ʿaṭf on «فأصَّدَّقَ», and «فأصَّدَّقَ» is accusative as the answer to the wish in His saying «لولا أَخَّرتني». The others read «وأكُنْ» jussive, the wāw having been dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The people's expressions differed on this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "By ʿaṭf on the position of «فأصَّدَّقَ», as if it had been said: 'If You delay me, I will give charity and be.'" Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "By ʿaṭf on the position (ʿalā l-mawḍiʿ), because the implied form is: 'if You delay me, I will give charity and be'. This is the position of Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī. As for what Sībawayh reported from al-Khalīl, it is other than this: it is a jussive on the supposition (tawahhum) of the condition that the wish points to, and there is no 'position' here because the condition is not apparent; ʿaṭf on the position is made only where the condition appears, as in His saying {مَن يُضْلِلِ الله فَلاَ هَادِيَ لَهُ وَيَذَرُهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 186], where whoever put it in the jussive made it a ʿaṭf on the position of {فَلاَ هَادِيَ لَهُ}, because if a verb were to occupy its place it would be jussive." End. What he reported from Sībawayh is the well-known view among the grammarians. Sībawayh gave a parallel to it in the saying of Zuhayr: 4268 - بَداليَ أني لَسْتُ مُدْرِكَ ما مَضَى ... ولا سابقٍ شيئاً إذا كان جائيا
(It appeared to me that I am not one to overtake what has passed, nor one to outstrip anything when it comes.)
He put «ولا سابقٍ» in the genitive by ʿaṭf on «مُدْرِكَ», which is the khabar of laysa, on the supposition that the bāʾ was added to it, because the khabar of laysa is frequently made genitive by an added bāʾ. This is the reverse of the noble verse, since in the verse the jussive was on the supposition of the fāʾ's omission, and here the genitive is on the supposition of the bāʾ's presence; but what joins them is the supposition of what would make that permissible. But I do not like this expression to be used for the Qur'ān, so it is not said "jussive by supposition", for its ugliness in wording. Abū ʿUbayd said: "I saw it in the codex of ʿUthmān as «وأكُنْ» without a wāw." The Shaykh distinguished between ʿaṭf on the position and ʿaṭf on the supposition by something, saying: "The difference between them is that the governor in ʿaṭf on the position is present and its effect absent, while the governor in ʿaṭf on the supposition is absent and its effect present." End. I say: an example of the first is «هذا ضاربُ زيدٍ وعمراً»; this is ʿaṭf on the position, the governor, namely «ضارب», is present and its effect, namely the accusative, is absent. An example of the second is what we have in hand; for the governor of the jussive is absent and its effect present. Plainer than it is Zuhayr's verse, for the bāʾ is absent and its effect present, but its effect appeared only in the conjoined and not in that to which it is conjoined, and likewise in the noble verse. Of this kind is the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4269 - فظلَّ طُهاةُ اللحمِ مِنْ بينِ مُنْضِجٍ ... صَفيفِ شِواءٍ قَديرٍ مُعَجَّلِ
(And the meat-cooks spent the day, some cooking slices of roast, and others stewing it, hurrying.)
They made it a case of ʿaṭf on supposition; that is, he supposed he had put «منضج» in iḍāfa to «صَفيف», and had he put it in iḍāfa to it, he would have made it genitive, so he conjoined «قدير» to «صفيف» in the genitive, supposing its being made genitive by iḍāfa.
ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «وأكونُ» with the verb in the nominative, as resumptive, that is, "and I shall be", and this is a promise on his part of righteousness.

semin-durr:11-11.t: Abū Bakr read «بما يعملون» in the third person, and the others in the second person, and both are clear. Ubayy, ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ibn Jubayr read «فأَتَصَدَّقَ», which is the original of the reading of the majority, except that the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنْفِقُوا مِنْ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلَا أَخَّرْتِنِي إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (١٠))
His saying (وَأَكُونَ): in the accusative, conjoined to what precedes it, which is the answer to the interrogative. It is also read in the jussive [وَأَكُنْ], construed according to the meaning; the meaning is "if You defer me, I will be (أَكُنْ)". And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ أَجْسَامُهُمْ وَإِنْ يَقُولُوا تَسْمَعْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ هُمُ الْعَدُوُّ فَاحْذَرْهُمْ قَاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ (٤))
His saying (كَأَنَّهُمْ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in «قَوْلِهِمْ».
It is also said: it is resumptive.
And (خُشُبٌ), with ḍamma and with sukūn [خُشْبٌ], is the plural of خَشَبٍ, like أَسَدٍ and أُسُدٍ. It is also read with two fatḥas [خَشَبٌ], the singular being خَشَبَةٌ. And يَحْسَبُونَ is a ḥāl from the meaning of the sentence; it is also said: resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ لَوَّوْا رُءُوسَهُمْ وَرَأَيْتَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ (٥)) (سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ لَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفَاسِقِينَ (٦))
His saying (رَسُولُ اللَّهِ): what governs it is «يَسْتَغْفِرْ»; had تَعَالَوْا been made to govern it, He would have said "to the Messenger of Allah (إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ)", or it would have been put in the accusative. And (لَوَّوْا) is read with a light [wāw] and with a doubled one, and that is evident.
The hamza in «أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ» has fatḥa; it is a disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ), and the conjunctive hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) is dropped. Some read it with waṣl, on the view that the interrogative was omitted because أَمْ indicates it.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَقُولُونَ لَئِنْ رَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا الْأَذَلَّ. . . (٨))
His saying (لَيُخْرِجَنَّ) is read with the agent named and with doubling [of the nūn]; «الْأَعَزُّ» is the fāʿil (agent) and «الْأَذَلَّ» the object. It is also read with the agent unnamed (passive) [لَيُخْرَجَنَّ]; on this reading الْأَذَلَّ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), the alif and lām being redundant (zāʾida); or it is the object of an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "resembling الْأَذَلَّ (the most humble)".

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn (The Hypocrites)
Medinan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إذا جاءَكَ المُنافِقُونَ قالُوا نَشْهَدُ إنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ واللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إنَّ المُنافِقِينَ لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ — He declared them liars with respect to what their hearts believe, and in that they swear by Allah that they are of you, and swear by Allah that they did not say (it), when they had indeed said the word of disbelief.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أيْمانَهم جُنَّةً﴾ means: a screen by which they shield themselves from him; the proof of that is that they swore to what we have described. It was also read ”اِتَّخَذُوا إيمانَهُمْ“ with a kasra on the hamza, i.e. their outward display of faith — ﴿جُنَّةً فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾.

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿فَطُبِعَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ — it was also read ”فَطَبَعَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ“, and ”فَطَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ“ has been transmitted. The well-known reading agreed upon here is ”فَطُبِعَ“, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive). In Arabic it is permissible to say ”فَطُبِعْ عَّلى قُلُوبِهِمْ“, assimilating the ʿayn into the ʿayn, because the two share a single point of articulation, and because of the accumulation of vowels, since six vowels come together. Whoever leaves out the assimilation does so because the two letters are in two words, and because the ʿayn is a letter of the throat, and assimilation is more frequent among the letters of the mouth than among the letters of the throat — such as ”مَدَّ“, ”شَدَّ“, ”قَرَّ“ and ”رَدَّ“ — being more frequent than the type ”دَعَّهُ، يَدُعُّهُ“.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذا رَأيْتَهم تُعْجِبُكَ أجْسامُهم وإنْ يَقُولُوا تَسْمَعْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ﴾ — it is as though He described them as having perfect forms and fine eloquence; then He made known that in their neglect of understanding and seeking insight they are like timber, and said: ﴿كَأنَّهم خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ﴾. It is also read ”خُشْبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ“ with the shīn quiescent. Whoever reads with the shīn quiescent treats it like ”بَدَنَةٌ“ / ”بُدْنٌ“; and whoever says ”خُشُبٌ“ with a ḍamma on the shīn treats it like ”ثَمَرَةٌ“ / ”ثُمُرٌ“. ”خَشَبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ“ is also permissible, but do not recite it unless a transmission of it is established; ”خَشَبَةٌ“ / ”خَشَبٌ“ is like ”شَجَرَةٌ“ / ”شَجَرٌ“.

His saying: ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — Allah the Exalted described them as cowardly; the case of everyone who addressed the Prophet ﷺ would be (taken by them to mean) that he was addressing him only about their affair, to expose their hypocrisy. [Translator's note: the words "taken by them to mean" are added for clarity; the Arabic sentence is elliptical.]

His saying: ﴿هُمُ العَدُوُّ فاحْذَرْهُمْ﴾ means: they are the nearest enemy, so beware of them, because they were enemies of the Prophet ﷺ while making a show of being with him.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ أنّى يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ — the meaning of ”أنّى يُؤْفَكُونَ“ is: from where are they turned away from the truth to falsehood?!

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهم تَعالَوْا يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكم رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ — Abū ʿAmr read ”يَسْتَغْفِر لَّكُمْ“, assimilating the rāʾ into the lām, which according to Sībawayh is not permissible; we have explained that in Sūrat ”اَلصَّفِّ“ (al-Ṣaff).

His saying: ﴿لَوَّوْا رُءُوسَهُمْ﴾ — on the pattern ”فَعَّلُوا“; it was also read ”لَوَوْا رُؤُوسَهُمْ“, undoubled. It is said that this was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿هُمُ الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لا تُنْفِقُوا عَلى مَن عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ حَتّى يَنْفَضُّوا﴾ — this too was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy. That was because he said to some people who were spending on some of those with the Messenger of Allah: "Do not spend on them, so that they disperse from him." ﴿وَلِلَّهِ خَزائِنُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ ولَكِنَّ المُنافِقِينَ لا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ means: Allah provides for them, and He is their provider even while these are spending on them.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَقُولُونَ لَئِنْ رَجَعْنا إلى المَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ الأعَزُّ مِنها الأذَلَّ﴾ — they also mean ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy. [Translator's note: so in the text; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy is usually identified as the speaker of these words, not their referent.] So Allah made known that He will make His religion prevail over all religion and will grant might to His Messenger and the believers with him, and He said: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ العِزَّةُ ولِرَسُولِهِ ولِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُلْهِكم أمْوالُكم ولا أوْلادُكم عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ — Allah urged them to keep up His remembrance continually and not to be miserly with their wealth, and said: ﴿وَأنْفِقُوا مِن ما رَزَقْناكم مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَأْتِيَ أحَدَكُمُ المَوْتُ﴾ [al-Munāfiqūn: 10], i.e. before he beholds that by which he knows he is dying, ﴿فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلا أخَّرْتَنِي إلى أجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأصَّدَّقَ وأكُنْ مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [al-Munāfiqūn: 10]. It was also read ”فَأصَّدَّقَ وأكُونَ مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ“. It has come in the exegesis that no one falls short in zakāt or in the Hajj without asking to be sent back. Whoever says ﴿فَأصَّدَّقَ وأكُنْ مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [al-Munāfiqūn: 10]: ”فَأصَّدَّقَ“ is the jawāb (answer) to ”لَوْلا أخَّرْتَنِي“, whose meaning is "Why did You not delay me?", and the jussive of ”وَأكُن“ is (in agreement) with the position of ﴿فَأصَّدَّقَ﴾ [al-Munāfiqūn: 10], because it has the sense: "If You delay me, I will give charity and be among the righteous." And whoever read ”وَأكُونَ“, that is (in agreement) with the overt form of ”فَأصَّدَّقَ“: ”فَأصَّدَّقَ وأكُونَ“.
